stubborn, obstinate, restive (as a horse); (अस्), m. a wicked wretch, reprobate, ruffian; N. of a sage (associated with Dur-vāsas, Kaṇva, Kātyāyana). —दुर्विनीतक = दुर्-विनीत. —दुर्-विपाक, अस्, m. a bad end or result, evil consequences of acts done either in this or a former birth. —दुर्-विभाग, आस्, m. pl. ‘difficult to be disunited,’ N. of a people. —दुर्-विभाव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be conceived, incomprehensible, inconceivable. —दुर्-विभाष, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be pronounced or uttered; (अम्), n. harsh or offensive words, abuse. —दुर्-विमोचन, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be set free or liberated; (अस्), m., N. of one of the 100 sons of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra. —दुर्-विरो-चन, अस्, m. ‘shining badly (?),’ N. of one of the 100 sons of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra. —दुर्-विलसित, अम्, n. a rude or ill-mannered trick, rudeness, naughtiness, a wayward act; [cf. दुर्-लसित।] —दुर्-विवक्तृ, ता, त्री, तृ, declaring badly, answering wrongly. —दुर्-विवाह, अस्, m. a bad marriage, mesalliance. —दुर्-विश, अस्, आ, अम्, hard to be entered, difficult to be trod or walked upon. —दुर्-विष, अस्, आ, अम्, bad-tempered (?); ill-natured, malignant; (अस्), m. an epithet of Śiva. —दुर्-विषह, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be borne or supported, intolerable, in-supportable, difficult to be subdued or overcome, irresistible; difficult to be performed; (अस्), m. an epithet of Śiva; N. of one of the 100 sons of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra; (also read दुर्-विसह; cf. दुः-षह, दुः-सह, दुष्-प्रसह।) —दुर्-विषह्य, अस्, आ, अम्, = दुर्-विषह. —दुर्-वृत्त, अम्, n. bad conduct, misconduct, ill-behaviour, mean practices; (अस्, आ, अम्), behaving badly, misbehaved, vile, wicked, criminal, leading a low or infamous life, following disreputable habits or business, cheating, roguish, a cheat, rogue, blackguard. —दुर्-वृत्ति, इस्, f. bad circumstances, distress, misery, want, indi-gence; disreputable conduct, bad practices; fraud. —दुर्-वृष्टि, इस्, f. insufficient rain, drought, dryness, aridity. —१। दुर्-वेद, अस्, आ, अम् (rt. 1. विद्), having bad or little knowledge, unlearned; difficult to be known. —२। दुर्-वेद, अस्, आ, अम् (rt. 3. विद्), difficult to be found. —दुर्-व्यवस्थापक, अस्, आ, अम्, deciding badly, giving a bad or unfavourable judgment. —दुर्-व्यवहार, अस्, m. a wrong judg-ment (in law). —दुर्-व्याहृत, अस्, आ, अम्, spoken badly or ill; (अम्), n. a bad or unfit expression. —दुर्-व्रजित, अस्, m. a bad or improper gait, bad manner of going. —दुर्-व्रत, अस्, आ, अम्, disobe-dient, not conforming to rules; [cf. दौर्व्रत्य।] —दुर्-हण or दुर्-हन, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. difficult to be killed, difficult to be destroyed or overcome, hard to be overpowered, irresistible; (णा), f., Ved. ill luck, misfortune. —दुर्हणायत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, or दुर्हणायु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. seeking to destroy, intending injury, meditating evil or damage. —दुर्-हणा-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. fatal, pernicious. —दुर्-हणु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. having deformed jaws. —दुर्-हन, see दुर्-हण. —दुर्-हार्द्, त्, त्, त्, Ved. ill-disposed; [cf. दुर्-हृद् and दौर्हार्द।] —दुर्-हित, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. unfriendly, hostile, trouble-some. —दुर्-हुत, अम्, n. a badly offered sacrifice. —दुर्-हृणायत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, or दुर्हृणायु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. whose fury is difficult to restrain or be borne. —दुर्-हृद्, त्, त्, त्, bad-hearted, hard-hearted, ill-disposed, inimical; (त्), m. an enemy; [cf. दुर्-हार्द् and दौर्हार्द।] —दुर्-हृदय, अस्, आ, अम्, evil-minded, bad-hearted; [cf. दौर्-हृदय।] —दुर्-हृषीक, अस्, आ, अम्, having defective organs of sense, badly restraining the senses; [cf. दुर्बलेन्द्रिय and दुर्-बल।]
दुरस्य: दुरस्य (probably connected with 2. दुर्), Nom. P. दुरस्यति, &c., Ved. to wish to hurt, desire to injure.
दुरस्यु: दुरस्यु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. wishing to do harm, desirous of inflicting injury.
दुर: दुर 1. दुर, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. (according to Sāy. fr. rt. 1. दा), a giver, granter; (perhaps rather to be derived fr. rt. दॄ, one who opens, unlocks.)
दुर 2. दुर = 1. दुर् (occurring only in शत-दुर, q. v.). —दुर-दभ्न, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. deceiving or illuding doors, i. e. not to be kept in or restrained by bolts and bars.
दुरोण: दुरोण, अम्, n., Ved. residence, dwelling, home. —दुरोण-सद्, त्, त्, त्, Ved. residing in a house.
दुरोणायु: दुरोणायु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. fond of the house; (Sāy.) frequenting the sacrificial hall.
दुर्य: दुर्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. belonging to the door or house; (आस्), m. or f. pl. a residence; (perhaps ‘the posts of the door;’ cf. Lat. fores.)
दुर्योण: दुर्योण, अम्, n., Ved. a residence, dwelling-place, = दुरोण (?); Sāy. = सङ्ग्राम, battle, or (दुस् + योनि) = दुर्योनि, N. of a king.
दुराक: दुराक दुराक, अस्, m., N. of a barbarous tribe.
दुरु: दुरु दुरु, उस्, m., N. of a mountain.
दुरुःफ: दुरुःफ दुरुःफ, (in astrology) N. of the fifteenth Yoga; (also read दुरफ and दुरुफ।)
दुरुधरा: दुरुधरा दुरुधरा, f. (a word borrowed fr. the Gr. δορυφορία), a peculiar position of the moon.
दुरोदर: दुरोदर दुरोदर, अस्, m. (probably for दरोदर, q. v., and connected with rt. दॄ; accord-ing to others perhaps fr. दुरस्, acc. pl. of 1. दुर्, q. v., + दर, piercing or breaking the doors; cf. दुर-दभ्न under 2. दुर), one who plays at dice, a gamester; a dice-box; a stake; (अम्), n. (according to a commentator also अस्, m.), playing, gaming, a game at dice.
दुर्दर: दुर्दर, अस्, आ, अम् (probably for दर्दर, q. v.), tearing; distressing; a kind of drug, = ऋषभ; [cf. दरिद्र and दुर्-धर।]
दुर्ग: दुर्ग दुर्-ग, दुर्-गा, &c. See p. 420, col. 3.
दुर्दुरूट: दुर्दुरूट दुर्दुरूट or दुर्दुरुट, अस्, m. (said to be fr. 2. दुर्, ‘vile,’ repeated), an expression of reproach; an atheist, = करट।
दुर्धुरूट: दुर्धुरूट or दुर्धुरुट, अस्, m. a pupil who does not obey his teacher without exercising his own judgment.
दुर्द्रिता: दुर्द्रिता दुर्द्रिता, f. a kind of creeping plant.
दुर्व्: दुर्व् दुर्व्, cl. 1. P. दूर्वति, &c., to hurt, injure, kill; [cf. rt. धुर्व्।]
दुर्वारि: दुर्वारि दुर्वारि, अयस्, m. pl., N. of a tribe of the Kāmbojas.
दुल्: दुल् दुल्, cl. 10. P. दोलयति, &c., to swing, heave upwards, raise, throw up, whirl, shake to and fro, cause to oscillate or vibrate, excite; [cf. तुल्, दोल, दोलाय।]
दुला: दुला, f., Ved. ‘shaking,’ N. of an Iṣṭakā or sacrificial brick.
दुलयते: दुलयते दुल्-अयते = दुर्-अयते। See दुर्-इ, p. 420, col. 2.
दुलि: दुलि दुलि, इस्, m., N. of a Muni or saint; (इस्, ई), f. a small or female tortoise; [cf. दौलेय।]
दुलिदुह: दुलिदुह दुलिदुह, अस्, m., N. of a prince; of a son of An-amitra and father of Dilīpa.
दुवन्य: दुवन्य दुवन्य (perhaps fr. rt. 1. दु), Ved. worshipping. —दुवन्य-सद्, त्, त्, त्, Ved. (Sāy.) dwelling among worshippers, abiding with the de-vout; [cf. दुवस् below.]
दुवस्: दुवस्, अस्, n., Ved. worship, honour, reverence; (Sāy.) wealth; (आस्, आस्, अस्), active, moving rest-lessly. —दुवस्-कृ, cl. 8. P. A. -करोति, -कुरुते, -कर्तुम्, to worship. —दुवस्-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. worshipping; enjoying or receiving worship. —दु-वो-धा, cl. 3. P. A. -दधाति, -धत्ते, -धातुम्, to worship.
दुवसन: दुवसन, अस्, आ, अम्, active, moving; (Sāy.) adorable, worthy of worship.
दुवस्य: 1. दुवस्य, Nom. P. दुवस्यति, &c., Ved. to honour, worship, celebrate, acknowledge, reward; to present with, give as a reward.
2. दुवस्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. (according to Sāy.) worthy of worship or honour.
दुवस्यु: दुवस्यु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. honouring, worshipping, respectful.
दुवोया: दुवोया, f., Ved. worship; (only occurring in inst. दुवोया, in worship.)
दुवोयु: दुवोयु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. honouring, worshipping; (उ), ind. reverently; out of acknowledgment.
दुश्: दुश् दुश्, euphonically substituted for दुस् in comp. like दुश्-चक्षस्। See bottom of col. 3.
दुश्चिक्य: दुश्चिक्य दुश्चिक्य, अम्, n. (in astrology) N. of the third lunar mansion.
दुष्: दुष् 1. दुष्, euphonically substituted for दुस् in दुष्-कर &c. See p. 425, col. 1.

दुष् 2. दुष्, cl. 4. P. (ep. also A.) दुष्-यति, -ते, दुदोष, दोक्ष्यति, अदुषत् (according to Vopa-deva also अदुक्षत्), दोष्टुम्, to become bad or corrupted, to be ruined, to perish, suffer damage, to be soiled; to be or become depraved or defiled or impure, to be violated (as a woman), to be contaminated by a crime, to sin, to commit a mistake, to be wrong; to be faithless or unchaste (as a wife): Caus. दूषयति (ep. also -ते), -यितुम्, to corrupt, spoil, make bad, cause to perish, hurt, destroy, lay waste, to make unclean or impure, to soil, defile, contaminate, vitiate, taint; to dishonour or violate (as a girl or the wife of another); to cause evil or misfortune (in astrology); to corrupt the morals, deprave, demoralize; to adulterate; to falsify; to rescind, abrogate, annul, retract; to object, refute, disprove; to find fault with, speak ill of, accuse, blame, abuse, contemn; (it is to be observed that दूष्यते, Pass. of the Caus., may often more cor-rectly be read where दुष्यते is given in the printed editions of epic poems, the sense of दूष्यते being the same; according to Pāṇ. VI. 4, 91, another form of the Caus., viz. दोषयति, &c., is optionally used in speaking of moral corruption, e. g. कामो दूषयति or दोषयति चित्तम्, lust corrupts the mind.)
दुष्ट: दुष्ट, अस्, आ, अम्, become bad, spoiled, cor-rupted, reduced to a bad state, injured, damaged, ruined, spoiled, vitiated, contaminated, diseased, tainted, infected, degraded; depraved; violated; corrupt, vicious, wicked; bad, evil; faulty, guilty, convicted, culpable; having evil intentions, ill-affected; roguish, low, vile; worthless; painful; (आ), f. a bad woman, a harlot, an unchaste woman; (अम्), n. sin, an offence, crime, guilt; a kind of Costus, Costus Speciosus, = कुष्ठ. —दुष्ट-गज, अस्, m. a vicious elephant. —दुष्ट-चरित्र, अस्, आ, अम्, ill-conducted. —दुष्ट-चारिन्, ई, इणी, इ, practising evil deeds, wicked, criminal. —दुष्ट-चेतस्, आस्, आस्, अस्, evil-minded, malevolent, bad-hearted. —दुष्ट-ता, f. or दुष्ट-त्व, अम्, n. badness, wickedness; per-versity, falsehood; contamination, defilement, viola-tion. —दुष्ट-धी, ईस्, ईस्, इ, or दुष्ट-बुद्धि, इस्, इस्, इ, having bad thoughts, evil-minded, evil-affected. —दुष्ट-भाव, अस्, आ, अम्, evil-natured, of a wicked or depraved nature, innately bad or wicked. —दुष्टभाव-ता, f. wickedness, innate depravity. —दुष्ट-मति, इस्, इस्, इ, evil-minded, wicked, depraved. —दुष्ट-मानस, अस्, ई, अम्, evil-minded, depraved in mind. —दुष्ट-वाच्, क्, क्, क्, speaking evil, uttering bad language. —दुष्ट-वृष, अस्, m. a bad or vicious ox, a strong but stubborn ox which refuses to draw. —दुष्ट-व्रण, अस्, m. a dull boil or sore, an obstinate tumor; a sinus. —दुष्टात्मन् (°ट-आत्°), आ, आ, अ, of a bad nature, evil-minded, wicked. —दुष्टान्वित (°ट-अन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, defiled, rendered impure.
दुष्टि: दुष्टि, इस्, f. corruption, corruptness, depravity.
दुष्टीय: दुष्टीय, Nom. P. दुष्टीयति, &c., to become bad or corrupted (?).
दुस्: दुस् दुस्, ind. (related to rt. 2. दुष्, and reckoned by Pāṇini among the Upa-sargas), a particle and prefix to nouns and rarely to verbs, implying evil, bad, badly, wicked, wickedly, difficult, hard, with difficulty, slight, inferior, &c., and sometimes equiva-lent to the English prefix इन्- or उन्-; [cf. rt. 2. दुष्; rt. 1. द्विष्: Zend dush, dus-mananh, dush-i-ti: Gr. δυς e. g. δυσ-μενής: Goth. tus in tuz-veryan: Old Germ. zur-: Hib. do, do-dhail, ‘bad luck;’ do-dhuine, ‘a bad man;’ do-dheanta, ‘hard to be done;’ do-bhasuighte, ‘immortal.’] दुस् becomes दुर्, q. v., before vowels and soft consonants; becomes दू, q. v., before र्; remains unchanged before त्, थ् (not however in the earlier language where स् becomes ष् and the following त्, थ् are changed to ट्, ठ्); becomes दुष् and rarely दुः before क्, ख् [cf. दुः-ख], प्, फ्; becomes दुः and rarely दुस्, दुश्, दुष् before स्, श्, and ष्। Those compounds in which दुस् becomes दुर् and दू will be found under दुर् and दू respectively. The other compounds formed with दुस् are as follow. —दुः-पच, दुः-पतन, दुः-पत्त्र, दुः-प्रज्ञ, &c., see दुष्-पच, &c., p. 425, col. 2. —दुः-शंस, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. wishing evil, malevolent, malicious, wicked. —दुः-शक or दुः-शक्त, अस्, आ, अम्, or दुः-शक्ति, इस्, इस्, इ, having no power, possessed of little power, powerless. —दुः-शल, अस्, m., N. of one of the 100 sons of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra; (आ), f., N. of the only daughter of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra, (she was the wife of king Jayad-ratha.) —दुः-शस्त, अस्, आ, अम्, badly recited; (अम्), n. a bad recitation. —दुः-शाक, अम्, ind. the luckless Śākas (see Pāṇ. II. 1, 6). —दुः-शास, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be controlled. —दुः-शासन, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be governed, intractable, difficult to be managed; (अस्), m., N. of one of the 100 sons of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra. —दुः-शासु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. wishing evil, malevolent. —दुः-शीम, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. = दुष्-प्राप, difficult to be attained; (अस्), m., N. of a man?; [cf. सु-शीम।] —दुः-शील, अस्, आ, अम्, badly disposed, ill-behaved, reprobate, abandoned. —दुःशील-ता, f. bad behaviour, badness of disposi-tion. —दुः-शृङ्गी, f. a disloyal wife. —दुः-शेव, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. ‘badly propitious,’ envious; (Sāy.) difficult to serve (as if सेव); delighting in evil. —दुः-शोध, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be cleaned. —दुः-शोष, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be dried. —दुः-श्रुत, अस्, आ, अम्, badly or wrongly heard. —दुः-षन्त, अस्, m., N. of the father of Bharata; [cf. दौःषन्ति; later forms are दुष्-मन्त, दुष्यन्त, दुष्वन्त, दुःष्वन्त।] —दुः-षम, अस्, आ, अम्, unlike, uneven; adverse, unlucky, unfortunate; wrong; (अम्), ind. unevenly, improperly; at a wrong time; (आ), f. (with Jainas) N. of two spokes in the wheel of time, viz. the fifth in the Ava-sarpiṇī, and the second in the Ut-sarpiṇī; [cf. दुः-सम।] —दुःषम-सुषमा, f. ‘both unfortunate and fortunate’ (but with a preponderance of misfortune), N. of two spokes in the Jaina wheel of time, viz. the fourth in the Ava-sarpiṇī, and the third in the Ut-sarpiṇī. —दुः-षह, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. difficult to be borne, irresistible; [cf. दुः-सह।] —दुः-षुप्त, अस्, आ, अम्, sleeping badly, having bad dreams. —दुः-ष्टुत and दुः-ष्टुति, see दु-ष्टुत, दु-ष्टुति, p. 425, col. 2. —दुः-ष्वप्न्य, अम्, n., Ved. ‘causing bad dreams,’ evil dream, pain; (Sāy.) poverty; [cf. जाग्र-द्°, स्वप्न-द्°, दौः-ष्वप्न्य, दुः-स्वप्न।] —दुः-संलक्ष्य, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be observed or recognised. —दुः-संस्कार, अस्, m. a bad custom or practice. —दुः-सक्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, or दुः-सक्थि, इस्, इस्, इ, having deformed thighs. —दुः-सङ्ग, अस्, m. bad inclina-tion, evil attachment. —दुः-सञ्चार, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be passed. —दुः-सञ्चिन्त्य, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be conceived or imagined. —दुः-सत्त्व, अम्, n. an evil being, noxious creature, ferocious animal. —दुःसत्त्व-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, filled with or infested by evil beings or ferocious animals. —दुः-सन्तुष्ट, अस्, आ, अम्, unsatisfied, discontented. —दुः-सन्धान or दुः-सन्धेय, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be joined together or united or reconciled. —दुः-सम, अस्, आ, अम्, unequal, uneven, unlucky, unfit, improper, evil, bad, unseasonable; [cf. दुः-षम।] —दुः-समतिक्रम, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be surmounted, insurmountable. —दुः-समी-क्ष्य, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be observed or per-ceived. —दुः-सम्पाद or दुः-सम्पाद्य, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be reached or attained. —दुः-सह, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be borne, unbearable, irresistible; (अस्), m., N. of one of the 100 sons of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra; of a son of Puru-kutsa and father of Sam-bhūti; of an evil demon; (आ), f. an epithet of Śrī; N. of a shrub (= नाग-दमनी); [cf. दुः-षह, दुर्-विषह, दुष्-प्रसह।] —दुः-स-हाय, अस्, आ, अम्, having evil companions or asso-ciates. —दुः-साक्षिन्, ई, m. a false witness. —दुः-साध्य, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be accomplished; difficult to be managed; difficult to be cured; diffi-cult to be conquered. —दुः-सेव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, diffi-cult to be used or dealt with, hard to be managed, intractable. —दुः-स्त्री, f. a bad woman. —दुः-स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘standing badly,’ badly fixed, unsteady, disquieted; badly circumstanced, suffering pain or affliction, distressed, unhappy; unwell, ill, badly situated, ill-conditioned, poor, miserable; igno-rant, unwise, a fool; (अम्), ind. badly, ill, unwell; in bad circumstances. —दुः-स्थित, अस्, आ, अम्, = दुः-स्थ above; (अम्), n. an improper manner of standing. —दुः-स्थिति, इस्, f. instability, unsteadi-ness; ill condition, bad fortune, unhappiness. —दुः-स्थेय, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be stood; (अम्), n. difficult standing or position. —दुः-स्नान, अम्, n. defective or inauspicious ablution. —दुः-स्पर्श, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult or unfit to be touched or laid hold of, unpleasant to the touch; (अस्), m. the prickly plant Alhagi Maurorum (= लता-करञ्ज); (आ), f., N. of several plants, Solanum Jacquini [cf. क्षुद्र-द्°]; Alhagi Maurorum, Mucuna Pruritus, Cassyta Filiformis. —दुः-स्पृश, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be touched; [cf. दुः-स्पर्श।] —दुः-स्पृष्ट or दु-स्पृष्ट, अम्, n. slight contact, the slight action of the tongue which produces the sounds य्, र्, ल्, व्; (अस्), m. a sound produced by this slight motion of the tongue. —दुः-स्फोट, अस्, m. ‘difficult to be burst,’ a sort of weapon. —दुः-स्वन, अस्, आ, अम्, sounding badly, cacophonous. —दुः-स्वप्न, अस्, m. a bad dream. —दुःस्वप्न-दर्शन, अस्, आ, अम्, seeing a bad dream. —दुःस्वप्न-नाश, अस्, m. the removal of bad dreams. —दुःस्वप्न-नाशन, अस्, आ, अम्, removing bad dreams. —दुःस्वप्न-प्रतिबोधन, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be awakened from sleep. —दुःस्वप्नोपशान्ति (°न-उप्°), इस्, f. the cessa-tion of a bad dream. —दुश्-चक्षस्, आस्, आस्, अस्, Ved. evil-eyed. —दुश्-चर्, cl. 1. P. -चरति, -रितुम्, to act wrongly or badly towards (with acc. of person), to behave badly. —दुश्-चर, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be gone to or approached, unattainable, inaccessible, difficult to be passed or spent (as time); difficult to be performed or accom-plished; going with trouble or difficulty; acting ill, behaving wickedly; (अस्), m. a bear (as moving slowly); a bivalve shell. —दुश्चर-चारिन्, ई, इणी, इ, practising very difficult penance. —दुश्चर-त्व, अम्, n. inaccessibility, difficulty of being approached or practised. —दुश्-चरित, अस्, आ, अम्, misbehaving, wicked, abandoned; (अम्), n. misbehaviour, misdoing, ill-conduct, wickedness; (आनि), n. pl. (with Buddhists) the ten chief sins, viz. murder, theft, adultery, lying, calumny, lewdness, evil speech, covetousness, envy, heresy. —दुश्चरितिन्, ई, इनी, इ, performing wicked actions. —दुश्-चर्मन्, आ, आ, अ, affected with disease of the skin, leprous; a circumcised man, one whose prepuce is naturally or artificially wanting; [cf. दौश्चर्म्य।] —दुश्-चारित्र, अस्, आ, अम्, or दुश्-चारिन्, ई, इणी, इ, badly conducted, misbehaving. —दुश्-चिकित्स, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be cured, incurable. —दुश्-चिकित्सा, f. (in medic.) wrong treatment. —दुश्-चिकित्सित or दुश्-चिकित्स्य, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be cured. —दुश्चिकित्स्य-तम, अस्, आ, अम्, most difficult to be cured. —दुश्चिकित्स्य-त्व, अम्, n. difficulty of being cured, incurableness. —दुश्-चित्, त्, त्, त्, Ved. thinking evil. —दुश्-चिन्त्य, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be thought about or under-stood. —दुश्-चेष्टित, अस्, आ, अम्, misbehaving, doing or designing evil; (अम्), n. evil purpose or action, misconduct, error. —दुश्-च्यवन or दुश्-च्याव or दुश्-च्यावन, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be felled or brought to the ground, unshaken, unmov-able; (अस्), m. an epithet of Indra; (another etymo-logy for the latter meaning is based upon the legend, that Indra having raised his arm to hurl his thunder-bolt at Cyavana, had it fixed in that position by the curse of the saint.) —दुश्-छद, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘covering badly,’ forming a bad garment; difficult to be clothed, hardly covered, tattered. —दुश्-छिद्, त्, त्, त्, difficult to be cut or destroyed. —दुश्-छिन्न, अस्, आ, अम्, badly cut or separated, badly extracted. —दुष्-कर, अस्, आ or ई, अम्, difficult or hard to be done or performed or accomplished; difficult to be reached or attained; difficult, arduous (with inf., e. g. दुष्करं कर्तुम्, difficult to perform); difficult to be borne or supported; doing badly or with difficulty, acting badly, wicked, bad; (अम्), n. difficult or painful act, a difficult task, a difficulty; atmosphere, ether; the tree of plenty?; (अम्), ind. hardly, scarcely (with following यदि). —दुष्करकारि-ता, f. the state of experi-encing difficulties. —दुष्कर-कारिन्, ई, इणी, इ, ex-periencing difficulties, suffering what is hard to be borne. —दुष्कर-चर्या, f. ‘the performance of difficulties,’ N. of the seventeenth chapter of the Lalita-vistara which describes Śākya-muni as the performer of difficult tasks. —दुष्-करण, अम्, n. anything difficult to be done or performed, a diffi-cult task. —दुष्-कर्ण, अस्, m., N. of one of the 100 sons of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra; (also read दुः-कर्ण।) —दुष्-कर्मन्, अ, n. evil act, crime, wickedness, sin; any difficult or painful act; (आ, आ, अ), acting wickedly, wicked, criminal. —दुष्-कलेवर, अस्, अम्, m. n. ‘the bad or miserable body,’ i. e. the body considered as the seat of diseases &c. —दुष्-कायस्थ-कुल, अम्, n. the miserable writer-caste. —दुष्-काल, अस्, m. ‘bad or all-destroying time,’ an epithet of Śiva. —दुष्-कीर्त्ति, इस्, इस्, इ, dis-honourable. —दुष्-कुल, अम्, n. a low family or race; (अस्, आ, अम्), of a low family, low-born; [cf. दौष्कुल, दौष्कुलेय, दौष्कुल्य।] —दुष्-कुल-ता, f. lowness of origin, meanness of birth or family. —दुष्कुलीन, अस्, आ, अम्, of a low or degraded family or race, low-born; (अस्), m. a sort of perfume, commonly called Chora. —दुष्-कृत्, त्, त्, त्, Ved. an evil-doer, offender, wicked, criminal. —दुष्-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, done wrongly or wickedly, done with difficulty or pain, badly organized, badly applied (e. g. दुष्कृता पूजा, badly applied worship); (अम्), n. evil action, misdeed, sin, crime, guilt. —दुष्कृत-कर्मन्, आ, आ, अ, acting wickedly, wicked, reprobate, a criminal; (अ), n. a wicked deed, wickedness. —दुष्कृत-वहिष्कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, free from sin. —दुष्कृतात्मन् (°त-आत्°), आ, आ, अ, evil-minded, wicked, base. —दुष्-कृति, इस्, इस्, इ, or दुष्कृतिन्, ई, इनी, इ, acting wickedly, an evil-doer. —दुष्-कृष्ट, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. badly ploughed, ill-cultivated. —दुष्-क्रम, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult of access; going ill; ill-arranged, unme-thodical. —दुष्-क्रिया, f. evil act, a misdemeanour. —दुष्-क्रीत, अस्, आ, अम्, badly purchased, bought too dearly. —दुष्-ख, see दुःख at p. 418, col. 2. —दुष्-खदिर, अस्, m. a tree related to the Acacia Catechu (= खदिर). —दुष्-टनु, उस्, वी, उ, Ved. having an ugly body, having an odious form. —दुष्-टर, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. difficult to be crossed or passed, hard to be overcome, unconquer-able, invincible, irresistible; not to be subdued; not to be surpassed or excelled; difficult to be endured; [cf. the later form दुस्-तर।] —दुष्-टरीतु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. = दुष्-टर; (उस्), m. epithet of Indra; N. of a man. —दु-ष्टुत, अम्, n. (for दुः-ष्टुत), Ved. faulty recitation of the Stotra. —दु-ष्टुति, इस्, f. (for दुः-ष्टुति), Ved. a faulty or bad hymn. —दुष्ठु, उस्, उस्, उ (for दुः-स्थु), ‘standing badly,’ ill-behaved, depraved; (उ), ind. ill, bad; improperly, incorrectly; [cf. दौष्ठव and सु-ष्ठु।] —दुष्-पच, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be digested. —दुष्-पतन, अम्, n. falling badly, (formed to explain अप-भ्रंश।) —दुष्-पत्त्र, अस्, m. a kind of perfume, commonly called Chora; (also read दुः-पत्त्र।) —दुष्-पद, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. (according to Sāy. = दुष्-प्रपदन), not to be reached or overtaken. —दुष्-पराजय, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be conquered; (अस्), m., N. of one of the 100 sons of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra. —दुष्-परिग्रह, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be seized or kept. —दुष्-परिणाम, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be finished or ended. —दुष्-परिहन्तु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. difficult to be destroyed or disturbed. —दुष्-परीक्ष्य, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be investigated or examined. —दुष्पर्श, see दुः-स्पर्श. —दुष्-पान, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be drunk. —दुष्-पार, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be crossed or passed over; difficult to be accomplished or performed. —दुष्-पार्ष्णिग्रह, अस्, आ, अम्, having a dan-gerous enemy in the rear; (also read दुः-पार्ष्णि-ग्राह।) —दुष्-पीत, अस्, आ, अम्, badly drunk. —दुष्-पुत्र, अस्, m. a bad son. —दुष्-पुरुष, अस्, m. a bad man; (also read दुः-पुरुष; cf. दौष्पुरुष्य।) —दुष्-पूर, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be filled or satiated or satisfied. —दुष्-प्रकम्प or दुष्-प्रकम्प्य, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be shaken or agitated, immovable. —दुष्-प्रकाश, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘lighting badly,’ obscure, dark. —दुष्-प्रकृति, इस्, इस्, इ, evil-natured, bad-tempered. —दुष्-प्रजस्, आस्, आस्, अस् (प्रजस् = प्रजा), hav-ing bad offspring. —दुष्-प्रज्ञ, अस्, आ, अम्, having a weak intellect, weak-minded, stupid; [cf. दुःप्रज्ञ।] —दुष्प्रज्ञ-त्व, अम्, n. stupidity. —दुष्-प्रज्ञान, अम्, n. want of understanding, weak intellect; (अस्, आ, अम्), Ved. weak in intellect, stupid. —दुष्-प्रणीत, अस्, आ, अम्, badly led, badly conducted or trained, ill-managed; (अम्), n. im-prudent or impolitic conduct; ill luck, evil fortune; [cf. दुर्-नीत।] —दुष्-प्रतर, अस्, आ, अम्, diffi-cult to be passed over or crossed. —दुष्-प्रतिग्रह, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be taken or laid hold of. —दुष्-प्रतिवारण, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be warded off or averted. —दुष्-प्रतिवीक्षणीय or दुष्-प्रतिवीक्ष्य, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be looked at, one whose glance is unbearable. —दुष्-प्र-धर्ष, अस्, आ, अम्, not to be assailed or meddled with; difficult to be attacked; secure from assaults, intangible, not to be touched; (अस्), m., N. of one of the 100 sons of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra; (आ), f., N. of two prickly plants which cannot be touched, = खर्जूरी, Phœnix Sylvestris; = दुर्-आलभा, Alhagi Maurorum; [cf. दुर्-आधर्ष and दुर्-धर्ष।] —दुष्-प्रधर्षण, अस्, ई, अम्, = दुष्-प्र-धर्ष; (अस्), m., N. of one of the 100 sons of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra; (ई), f., N. of the plant Melongena Incurva; [cf. वार्ताकी।] —दुष्-प्रधर्षिणी, f. (wrong form for दुष्-प्रधर्षणी, according to some) = कण्टकारी, = बृहती. —दुष्-प्रधृ-ष्य, अस्, आ, अम्, = दुष्-प्रधर्ष. —दुष्-प्र-पदन, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be overtaken or attained. —दुष्-प्रमय, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be measured, immeasurable. —दुष्-प्रलम्भ, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be deceived; (according to others) difficult of attainment. —दुष्-प्रवाद, अस्, m. calumnious report, slander, defamation. —दुष्-प्रवृत्ति, इस्, f. bad news, sad intelligence. —दुष्-प्रवेश, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be entered; (आ), f. a kind of tree, = कन्थारी. —दुष्-प्रसह, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be borne or supported or suffered, hard to endure or resist, irresistible; terrible, frightful; (अस्), m., N. of a Jaina teacher; [cf. दुष्-प्रसा-ह, दुर्-विषह, दुः-सह, दुः-षह।] —दुष्-प्रसाद or दुष्-प्रसादन, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be propitiated or conciliated or appeased. —दुष्-प्रसाधन (perhaps wrongly read for दुष्-प्र-सादन) or दुष्-प्रसाध्य, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be managed or dealt with (as a bad-tempered man). —दुष्-प्रसाह, अस्, आ, अम्, = दुष्-प्र-सह. —दुष्-प्रहर्ष, अस्, m. ‘bad rejoicing,’ N. of one of the 100 sons of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra. —दुष्-प्राप or दुष्-प्रापण or दुष्-प्राप्य, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult of attainment, hard to attain, difficult to be reached, unattainable, remote. —दुष्-प्रावी, ईस्, ईस्, इ, Ved. difficult of access, unfavourable, un-friendly. —दुष्-प्रीति, इस्, f. displeasure. —दुष्-प्रेक्ष or दुष्-प्रेक्षणीय or दुष्-प्रेक्ष्य, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be looked at, disagreeable to the sight. —दुष्मन्त, अस्, m. another form for दुष्यन्त below; [cf. दौष्मन्त, दौष्मन्ति, सुष्मन्त।] —दुष्यन्त, अस्, m. (a later form for दुः-षन्त, q. v.), N. of a prince of the lunar line or descendant of Puru, husband of Śakuntalā and father of Bharata; [cf. दौष्यन्त and दौष्-यन्ति।] —दुष्वन्त, अस्, m. another form for दुष्यन्त, q. v.; [cf. दौष्वन्ति and दुः-ष्वन्त।] —दुष्वप्न्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. = दुः-ष्वप्न्य, q. v. —दुस्-तप, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be endured (as a penance). —दुस्-तर, अस्, आ, अम्, or दुस्-तरण, अस्, ई, अम्, or दुस्-तरणीय, or दुस्-तार, अस्, आ, अम्, or दुस्-तीर्ण, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be crossed or passed over, hard to be traversed, impassa-ble, hard to be subdued, invincible; [cf. the older form दुष्-टर।] —दुस्-तर्क, अस्, m. false reason-ing, bad reasoning, wrong argument. —दुस्तर्क-मूल, अस्, आ, अम्, founded on false or wrong reason-ing. —दुस्-तर्क्य, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be sup-posed or reasoned about. —दुस्-तोष, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be satisfied. —दुस्-त्यज or दुस्-त्याज्य, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be relinquished or quitted. —दुस्थ, दुस्थित, दुस्पृष्ट, see दुः-स्थ, दुः-स्पृष्ट।
दुस्सथ: दुस्सथ दुस्सथ, अस्, m. a cock; a dog; (perhaps for दुः-सक्थ।)
दुस्सनि: दुस्सनि दुस्सनि, इस्, m., N. of a man.
दुह्: दुह् 1. दुह् (connected with rt. तुह्), cl. 1. P. दोहति, दुदोह, अदुहत्, and अदोहीत्, to hurt, pain, give pain, distress, torment.

दुह् 2. दुह् (the original form of this rt. was probably दुघ्, cf. दुघ), cl. 2. P. A. दोग्धि, दुग्धे (2nd sing. धोक्षि, धुक्षे); Impf. P. अधोक् (1st du. अदुह्व); Impv. P. दोग्धु (2nd sing. दुग्धि, A. धुक्ष्व), दुदोह, दुदुहे (3rd pl. P. दुदुहुस्; Bhāg. -Purāṇa V. 15, 9, दु-दूहुस्), धोक्ष्यति, -ते, अधुक्षत्, अधुक्षत, and अदुग्ध: (Vedic and irregular forms are, दोग्-धे; धुक्षस्व; दुहाम्; 3rd sing. दुहे; 3rd pl. दुह्रे, दुहते, and दुह्रते; अदुह्रन्; दोहत्; दुहुस्; धुक्षन्, धुक्षत; दुहीयत्; part. दुहान and दुघान); Inf. दोग्धुम्, Ved. दोग्-धोस्, दोहसे, to milk; to milk out, squeeze out; to extract (as the juice of the Soma); to draw anything out of another thing (with two acc., e. g. प्राणान् दुहन्न् इवात्मानम्, as it were drawing the life out of himself); to make a profit or extract gain out of anything (with acc.); to enjoy; to give milk (A., in this sense also cl. 4. दुह्यति, -ते); to yield milk or any desired object (A.), to grant desires (A.): Pass. दुह्यते, Aor. अदोहि, to be milked, to be drawn or extracted from: Caus. P. दोहयति (rarely -ते), -यितुम्, Aor. अदूदुहत्, to cause to milk or to be milked, to cause to yield milk or any desired object; to milk, milk out from, extract: Desid. दुधुक्षति, -ते, to wish to milk, to wish to milk out or enjoy [cf. दुधुक्षु]: Intens. दोदुह्यते, दोदोग्धि; [cf. Goth. tiuhan; Them. tuh, tiuha, tauh, tuhum, ‘to draw:’ Angl. Sax. tucian, teon, teoge: Old Germ. ziuhan, ziug (gaziug), zaugyan: Mod. Germ. ziehen: Lat. duc-ere: Hib. diugaim, ‘I drink off;’ diughailfainn, ‘sucking:’ Scot. deog-hail, ‘to suckle.’]
3. दुह्, धुक्, क्, क्, (at the end of a comp.) milking, yielding milk; yielding, granting (e. g. काम-द्°, गो-द्°, घर्म-द्°, घृत-द्°, q. v.).
दुह: दुह, अस्, आ, अम्, (at the end of a comp.) milking; yielding, granting (e. g. काम-द्°, गो-द्°; cf. दुर्-दुहा).
दुहत्: दुहत्, अन्, अती, अत्, milking; yielding, granting, parting with.
दुहितृ: दुहितृ, ता, f. a daughter (either as drawing milk from the mother or as milking the cows, ‘the milk-maid of the family’); [cf. Zend dugh-dhar; Gr. θύγ-ά-τηρ; Goth. dauh-tar; Old Germ. toh-tar; Slav. dush-ti; Lith. duk-te† for dukter; the original form must have been dhugh-atar.] —दु-हितुः-पति, इस्, m. a daughter's husband, son-in-law. —दुहितृ-त्व, अम्, n. the state of being a daughter, the condition of a daughter. —दुहितृ-पति, इस्, m. a daughter's husband. —दुहितृ-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having a daughter, possessing a daughter.
दुह्य: दुह्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be milked, milkable.
दुह्यु: दुह्यु दुह्यु, a wrong form for द्रुह्यु।
दू: दू 1. दू, generally written दु। See 2. दु, p. 418, col. 2.
दू, ऊस्, ऊस्, उ, burning with eagerness (?) in अ-दू; (ऊस्), f. pain, distress. —दू-द, अस्, आ, अम्, giving pain, afflicting, harassing.

दू 2. दू at the beginning of some comps. = दुर् for दुस्, as in the following examples. —दू-डभ or दू-ऌअभ, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. दुर् for दुस् + लभ), difficult to be deceived, not to be deceived. —दू-डाश्, ट्, ट्, ट् (fr. दुर् for दुस् + दाश्), not offering oblations, not worshipping. —दू-डाश, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. = the preceding. —दू-ढी, ईस्, ईस्, इ (fr. दुर् for दुस् + धी), Ved. of an evil disposition. —दू-ढ्य, अस्, आ, अम्, incorrect form for the preceding. —दू-णश, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. दुस् + नश्), Ved. unattainable, inaccessible; [cf. दुर्-आश, दुर्-णश, दू-णाश।] —दू-णाश, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. दुस् + नाश, attainment), Ved. unattainable, inacces-sible [cf. दुर्-णश]; (अस्), m., N. of an Ekāha; (अस्, आ, अम्), (fr. नाश, destruction), imperishable, not to be destroyed, not ceasing, perpetual. —दू-रक्त, अस्, आ, अम्, badly coloured or dyed. —दू-रक्ष्य, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be guarded or preserved. —दू-राध, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be accom-plished. —दू-रूढ, अस्, आ, अम्, badly grown; badly or imperfectly cicatrized. —दूरूढ-त्व, अम्, n. the state of being badly grown; bad or imperfect cicatrization. —दू-रोह, अस्, आ, अम्, ascending or climbing with difficulty. —दू-रोहण, अस्, आ, अम्, difficult to be ascended; (अम्), n., N. of a difficult ritual recitation in which a verse is recited in seven ways, (first only one Pāda, then one half of the verse, then three Pādas, then the whole verse, then three Pādas again, then one half of the verse, and then one Pāda again.) —दूरोहणीय, अस्, आ, अम्, recited or recitable in the manner described above.
दूतक: 1. दूतक, अस्, m. a N. of Agni in the form of a forest conflagration; [cf. दव and दाव।]

2. दूतक, अस्, m. (for 1. see col. 1. under rt. 1. दू), a messenger, ambassador [cf. देव-द्°]; (इका), f. a female messenger, go-between, &c.; a gadding, gossiping, mischief-making woman; [cf. काम-द्°।]
दूतीका: दूतीका, f. = दूतिका under 2. दूतक above.
दूत्य: दूत्य, अम्, n. the rank or employment or office of an ambassador; an embassy, a message; [cf. दौत्य।]
दूप्र: दूप्र दूप्र, अस्, आ, अम्, strong.
दूर्: दूर् दूर्, N. of the Prāṇa or vital breath regarded as a deity.
दूर: दूर दूर, अस्, आ, अम् (probably connected with दूत and rt. 1. दु, but said to be fr. rt. इ with prefix दुर् and affix र, the rt. being then dropped, see Uṇ.-sūt. II. 20; compar. दवीयस्, superl. द-विष्ठ, q. v.), distant, far from (with abl. or gen.); remote, long (e. g. गत्वा दूरम् अध्वानम्, having gone a long journey), a long way off; (अम्), n. distance, farness, remoteness, a long way, a long distance. The various cases of दूर are used adverbially, as follow: (अम्), ind. far, to a distance, far away, far or distant from (with abl. or gen., e. g. ग्रामात् or ग्रामस्य दू-रम्, far from the village), to a great height, aloft, high above; to a great depth below, far below, deeply; highly, in a high degree; दूरं कृ, to make distant, distance, surpass, exceed; (एण), ind. far, in a distant place, from afar, by far, by a long way; (आत्), ind. from a distance, from afar, far from (with abl., e. g. दूराद् आवसथात्, far from the fire-temple), afar, in a remote degree; a long way back, from a remote period; (ए), ind. in a distant place, far, far away. —दूर-आदिश्, क्, क्, क् (for दूरे-आदिश्), Ved. announcing or proclaiming to a distance. —दूर-आधी, ईस्, ईस्, इ (for दूरे-आधी), whose thoughts are in the distance or far away. —दूर-उपब्दस् (for दूरे-उप्°), Ved. sounding to a dis-tance; (perhaps ind.) —दूर-ग, अस्, आ, अम्, going far or to a distance, receding, being far, remote. —दूर-गत, अस्, आ, अम्, gone far away. —दूर-गामिन्, ई, इनी, इ, going far; (ई), m. an arrow. —दूर-गृह, अस्, आ, अम्, whose house is distant. —दूर-ग्रहण, अम्, n. seizing or perceiving objects from afar (a supernatural faculty). —दूरङ्-करण, अस्, ई, अम्, making far, making distant, removing. —दूरङ्-गत, अस्, आ, अम्, gone to a distance, far removed, distant. —दूरङ्-गम, अस्, आ, अम्, going far away or to a distance; (आ), f., scil. भूमि, one of the ten stages in the life of a Śrā-vaka. —दूर-चर, अस्, आ, अम्, going to a distance, walking far off. —दूर-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, born in a distant place, a native of a distant place. —दूर-तर, अस्, आ, अम्, farther; (ए), ind. at some distance from, far from (with abl.). —दूर-तस्, ind. from afar, from a distance, at a distance from, aloof from, far off, afar, far, at a distance; [cf. अ-द्°।] —दूर-ता, f. or दूर-त्व, अम्, n. remoteness, distance, farness. —दूर-दर्शन, अस्, आ, अम्, far-seeing; to be seen only from afar; (अम्), n. long-sight-edness; foresight; (अस्), m. a vulture. —दूर-दर्-शिन्, ई, इनी, इ, far-seeing, long-sighted; (ई), m. a vulture, N. of a vulture who was prime-minister of Citra-varṇa; a Pandit, learned man, doctor, teacher; a prophet, seer, sage; [cf. दीर्घ-द्°।] —दूर-दृश्, क्, क्, क्, far-seeing, long-sighted; (क्), m. a vulture; a learned man. —दूर-दृष्टि, इस्, f. far-sightedness, long-sightedness; foresight, discernment. —दूर-पात, अस्, m. a long flight; falling from a great height; (अस्, आ, अम्), shooting from afar, discharging (missiles) from a distance; [cf. दूराप्°।] —दूर-पातन, अम्, n. the act of shooting to a distance, discharging (missiles) from afar. —दूरपाति-ता, f. or दूरपाति-त्व, अम्, n. state or property of taking a long flight. —दूर-पातिन्, ई, इनी, इ, flying far, having a long flight, flying a long way; one whose (arrows) fly far, discharging (missiles) to a distance; [cf. दूराप्° and दूरेषु-प्°।] —दूर-पात्र, अस्, आ, अम्, having a wide channel or bed (as a river). —दूर-पार, अस्, आ, अम्, having the opposite shore far off (as a river); very broad; difficult to be crossed, hard of attainment; (अस्), m. a broad river which is diffi-cult to be crossed; (आ), f. epithet of the Ganges; [cf. दुष्-पार।] —दूर-बन्धु, उस्, उस्, उ, having one's kinsmen distant, banished from wife and kindred. —दूर-भाज्, क्, क्, क्, possessing distance, distant. —दूर-भाव, अस्, m. farness, remoteness, distance. —दूर-भिन्न, अस्, आ, अम्, struck or wounded from a distance; wounded deeply. —दूर-भेद, अस्, m. striking from a distance. —दूर-मूल, अस्, m. a kind of grass, Saccharum Munjia (= मुञ्ज)। —दूरम्-भविष्णु, उस्, उस्, उ, and दूरम्-भा-वुक, अस्, आ, अम्, being far away, proceeding to a distance. —दूर-यायिन्, ई, इनी, इ, going far. —दूर-वर्तिन्, ई, इनी, इ, being in the distance, far removed. —दूर-वस्त्रक, अस्, आ, अम्, having the clothes removed, naked. —दूर-वासिन्, ई, इनी, इ, residing in a distant land, outlandish. —दूर-विदारितानन (°त-आन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, having the mouth stretched widely open. —दूर-विभिन्न, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘far-separated,’ unconnected by the ties of nature. —दू-र-विलम्बिन्, ई, इनी, इ, hanging far down. —दूर-वेधिन्, ई, इनी, इ, piercing or striking from afar, missile, projectile (as weapons &c.). —दूर-सं-स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, being in the distance, remote, dis-tant. —दूर-संस्थान, अम्, n. residing or residence at a distance. —दूर-सूर्य, अस्, आ, अम्, having the sun distant. —दूर-स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, or दूर-स्थित, अस्, आ, अम्, or दूर-स्थायिन्, ई, इनी, इ, situ-ated at a distance, standing afar off, remote, far off. —दूरस्थ-त्व, अम्, n. the state of being remote. —दूर-स्वर्ग, अस्, आ, अम्, having heaven distant. —दूराद्-आगत, अस्, आ, अम्, come from a distance. —दूरान्तर (°र-अन्°), अम्, n. a wide space, a long interval. —दूरान्तरित (°र-अन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, separated by a wide space. —दूरापात (°र-आप्°), अस्, m. shooting from afar, discharging from a distance; [cf. दूर-प्°।] —दूरापातिन् (°र-आप्°), ई, इनी, इ, shooting or discharging (missiles) from afar; [cf. दूर-प्°।] —दूराप्लाव (°र-आप्°), अस्, आ, अम्, jumping or leaping far. —दूरारूढ (°र-आर्°), अस्, आ, अम्, mounted high, advanced or reaching far, intense. —दूरार्थ (°र-अर्°), अस्, m. remote or recondite object. —दूरावस्थित (°र-अव्°), अस्, आ, अम्, standing or being afar off. —दूरी-करण, अम्, n. the act of making distant, removing, placing at a distance. —दूरी-कृ, cl. 8. P. A. -करोति, -कुरुते, -कर्तुम्, to make distant, remove to a distance, expel, banish, distance, exceed, excel. —दूरी-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, made distant, removed, placed to a dis-tance or afar off. —दूरी-भू, cl. 1. P. -भवति, -भवितुम्, to become distant, move away, retire, go back. —दूरी-भूत, अस्, आ, अम्, become distant, removed, remote, far off. —दूरे-अन्त, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. ending in the remote distance, boundless; (ए), f. du. epithet of heaven and earth. —दूरे-अमित्र, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. whose enemies are far away. —दूरे-अर्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. whose aim is far off; (Sāy.) going far or widely sought. —दूरे-गव्यूति, इस्, इस्, इ, Ved. whose range or sphere reaches to a distance or is in the distance. —दूरे-चर, अस्, आ, अम्, going or travelling far, being far away, distant, remote. —दूरे-त्य, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. दूरे with affix त्य, Pāṇ. IV. 2. 104), being far off, being distant, come from afar. —दूरे-दृश्, क्, क्, क्, Ved. visible in remote places, far-seeing. —दूरे-भा, आस्, आस्, अम्, Ved. shining to a distance. —दूरे-यम, अस्, आ, अम्, one from whom Yama the god of death is distant, one from whom he is far removed. —दूरेरितेक्षण (°र-ईरित-ईक्ष्°), अस्, आ, अम्, ‘one who sends his glances far apart,’ squinting, squint-eyed. —दूरे-वध, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. far-striking, hitting at a distance. —दूरे-श्रवस्, आस्, आस्, अस्, far-renowned; (आस्), m., see दौरेश्रवस। —दूरे-श्रुत, see दौरेश्रुत. —दूरेषुपातिन् (°र-इष्°), ई, इनी, इ, discharging or shooting arrows to a distance; [cf. दूर-पातिन्।] —दूरे-हेति, इस्, इस्, इ, whose arrows or missile weapons fly to a distance. —दूरोन्नमित (°र-उन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, raised aloft, stretched far out.
दूरक: दूरक, अस्, आ, अम्, remote, distant, &c., = दूर।
दूरक्त: दूरक्त दू-रक्त, दू-रक्ष्य, दू-रोह, &c. See 2. दू, p. 426, col. 1.
दूर्य: दूर्य दूर्य, अम्, n. feces, ordure; a kind of Curcuma (= शटी).
दूर्व: दूर्व दूर्व, अस्, m., N. of a prince who was son of Nṛpañ-jaya and father of Ṭimi.
दूर्वा: दूर्वा दूर्वा, f. (said to be fr. rt. दुर्व्), bent grass, panic grass, commonly Panicum Dactylon; [cf. अलि-द्°, गण्डा-द्°, ग्रन्थि-द्°।] —दूर्वा-काण्ड, अम्, n. a quantity or heap of Dūrvā grass. —दूर्वा-क्षी (°वा-अक्°), f., N. of the wife of Vṛka. —दूर्वा-वण or दूर्वा-वन, अम्, n. a thicket of Dūrvā grass. —दूर्वा-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, intertwined or joined with Dūrvā grass. —दूर्वाष्टमी (°वा-अष्°), f., N. of a festival on the eighth day of the light half of the month Bhādra on which the Dūrvā is worshipped as a deity. —दूर्वा-सोम, अस्, m. a species of Soma plant. —दूर्वेष्टका (°वा-इष्°), f. Dūrvā grass used like bricks in erecting an altar.
दूर्श: दूर्श दूर्श, अम्, n., Ved. a kind of woven cloth or vesture; [cf. दूश्य and दूष्य।]
दूलास: दूलास दूलास, अस्, m. (?), a bow.
दूलिका: दूलिका दूलिका and दूली, f. the indigo plant; [cf. तूली, दोला, तरु-दूलिका।]
दूश्य: दूश्य दूश्य, अम्, n. = दूष्य, a tent.
दूष: दूष दूष, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. the Caus. of rt. 2. दुष्), defiling, polluting, contaminating, corrupt-ing, (generally at the end of comp.; cf. कोर-द्° and पङ्क्ति-द्°।)
दूषक: दूषक, अस्, इका, अम्, making bad, corrupting, polluting, contaminating, vitiating, spoiling, violating, dishonouring, disgracing, seducing, making mischief, hurting [cf. चर्म-दूषिका]; committing an offence against, offending, trespassing; disfiguring; acting against a command or precept; an offender, a seducer, corrupter, any infamous or wicked person; sinful, wicked (as an action); वेदानां दूषकस्, one who vitiates or is a disparager of the Vedas; (इका), f. a pencil or paint-brush; impurity or secretion of the eyes, rheum of the eyes [cf. दूषीका]; a kind of rice.
दूषण: दूषण, अस्, ई, अम्, corrupting, spoiling, ruining, destroying, vitiating, contaminating, dishonouring, violating; offending against; counteracting [cf. अरा-ति-द्°, कृत्या-द्°, खर-द्°, विष-द्°]; (अस्), m., N. of a Rakṣas or Rākṣasa who was one of the generals of Rāvaṇa; of a Daitya slain by Śiva; (आ), f., N. of a deity, the wife of Bhauvana and mother of Tvaṣṭṛ; (अम्), n. the act of spoiling or corrupting, ruining, vitiating, contaminating, hurting; violating (a contract), breaking (an agreement), dishonouring or violating a woman; slighting, speaking ill of any one, abusing, finding fault, censuring, disparaging, blaming, detracting, throwing doubts upon, criticising, objecting, refuting, rendering suspected; objection, adverse argument; fault, defect, offence, guilt, sin, blame; [cf. अर्थ-द्° and दोष।] —दूषणारि (°ण-अरि), इस्, m. ‘the enemy of Dūṣaṇa,’ epithet of Rāma. —दूषणावह (°ण-आव्°), अस्, आ, अम्, occasioning guilt.
दूषणीय: दूषणीय, अस्, आ, अम्, corruptible, liable to be vitiated, &c., = दूष्य।
दूषयत्: दूषयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, making bad, corrupting, defiling, &c.
दूषयाण: दूषयाण, अस्, आ, अम्, vitiating, defiling, spoiling.
दूषयितृ: दूषयितृ, ता, त्री, तृ, or दूषयित्नु, उस्, उस्, उ, a corrupter, one who dishonours or deflowers or violates (a girl).
दूषि: दूषि, इस्, इस्, इ, (at the end of comp.) corrupting, ruining, destroying [cf. अराति-द्°, आत्म-द्°, कृत्या-द्°]; (इस्), f., Ved. a poisonous substance; (इस्, ई), f. = दूषिका, दूषीका, the rheum of the eyes. —दूषी-विष, अम्, n. a vegetable poison that ceases to act because it has become old or decomposed (दूषित). —दूषीविषारि (°ष-अरि), इस्, m. a kind of antidote. —दूष्य्-उदर, अम्, n. a disease of the abdomen caused by poisonous substances. —दूष्युदरिन्, ई, इणी, इ, affected with the above disease.
दूषित: दूषित, अस्, आ, अम्, corrupted, spoiled, conta-minated; violated, hurt, injured; demoralized; disgraced; blamed, censured; calumniated, falsely accused, often at the end of comp., see मन्यु-द्°, शत्रूपजाप-द्°; (आ), f. a girl who has been violated or deflowered.
दूषिन्: दूषिन्, ई, इणी, इ, corrupting, contaminating, violating.
दूषीका: दूषीका, f. the secretion or rheum of the eyes; [cf. दूषिका under दूषक, दूषि।]
दूष्य: दूष्य, अस्, आ, अम्, corruptible, liable to be corrupted or defiled or contaminated; liable to be ruined, to be seduced or dishonoured, deserving censure, condemnable; reprehensible, culpable, con-temptible, vile, bad; (अस्), m. a wicked man; (अम्), n. matter, pus, poison; (अम्), n. clothes or a kind of cloth; cotton, calico; a tent (in this sense perhaps for दूश्य; cf. दूर्श); (आ), f. an elephant's leathern girth; [cf. चूषा and कक्ष्या।] —दूष्य-युक्त, अस्, आ, अम्, associated with a vile rascal.
दूष्यत्: दूष्यत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, offending, insulting (for दूषयत् ?).
दूस: दूस दूस, अम्, n. (considered as an affix), milk, (occurring in अवि-दूस, q. v.)
दृ: दृ दृ, cl. 6. A. द्रियते, &c., to honour, worship, (only occurring with prep. आ; cf. आ-दृ at p. 120, col. 1.)
दृ|अ दृऌह। See दृढ, p. 427, col. 2.
दृंह्: दृंह् दृंह् (connected and sometimes identified with rt. दृह्), cl. 1. P. दृंहति, ददृंह, दृंहितुम्, to make firm, fix, strengthen, confirm; to make fast, fasten; to fortify; cl. 1. A. दृंहते, to be firm or fixed; to grow, increase: Caus. दृंहयति, -यितुम्: Desid. दिदृंहिषति: Intens. दरीदृंह्यते।
दृंहण: दृंहण, अम्, n., Ved. making firm or fast, strengthening, fastening, fortifying; means of strength-ening; [cf. केश-द्°।]
दृंहित: दृंहित, अस्, आ, अम्, made firm or fast, fixed, strengthened, fortified; grown, increased.
दृंहितृ: दृंहितृ, ता, त्री, तृ, Ved. one who makes firm, a strengthener.
दृढ: दृढ or Ved. दृऌह, अस्, आ, अम्, fixed, firm, hard, strong, solid, massive; firmly fastened, shut fast; tough; difficult to be bent (as a bow), compact; tight, close, dense, without interstices, (opposed to भिन्न); durable; confirmed, established; not giving way, stubborn; certain, sure, not subject to vacillations; secure; reliable; steady, persevering; great, intense, excessive, severe, violent, mighty, powerful, important; (in mathematics) reduced to the last term or smallest number by a common divisor; (अस्), m. a term in music; N. of a son of the thirteenth Manu; of one of the sons of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra; (आ), f., N. of a Buddhist goddess, ‘the goddess of the earth;’ (अम्), n. anything fixed or firm or solid; a stronghold, fortress; iron; (अम्), ind. firmly, fast, much, in a high degree, excessively; thoroughly, very well. —दृढ-कण्टक, अस्, m. ‘having hard thorns,’ a kind of plant, = क्षुद्र-फलक, commonly धलाङ्कदा; (आ), f. the wild date tree, Phœnix Sylvestris. —दृढ-काण्ड, अस्, m. ‘having a strong stem,’ a bamboo; (आ), f. a kind of creeping plant, = पाताल-गरुडी; (अम्), n. a kind of fragrant grass (= दीर्घ-रोहिषक). —दृढ-कारिन्, ई, इणी, इ, ‘acting firmly,’ resolute, persevering, determined. —दृढ-क्रोध, अस्, आ, अम्, having violent anger. —दृढ-क्षत्र, अस्, m. ‘having strong prowess,’ N. of one of the 100 sons of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra. —दृढ-क्षुरा, f. ‘having hard blades,’ a kind of grass, = वल्व-जा. —दृढ-गा-त्रिका, f. ‘having hard particles,’ granulated sugar. —दृढ-ग्रन्थि, इस्, m. ‘having hard knots,’ a bamboo. —दृढ-ग्राहिन्, ई, इणी, इ, seizing firmly, i. e. pursuing an object with untiring energy. —दृ-ढ-च्छद, अस्, m. ‘having hard leaves,’ a kind of fragrant grass, = दीर्घ-रोहिषक. —दृढ-च्युत or दृऌह-च्युत or दृढाच्युत, अस्, m., N. of a son of Agastya or author of a hymn of the Ṛg-veda; [cf. दार्ढ-च्युत।] —दृढ-ज्ञान, अम्, n. certain knowledge, firm conviction. —दृढ-तर, अस्, आ, अम्, firmer, harder. —दृढ-तरु, उस्, m. ‘the strong tree,’ Grislea Tomentosa (= धव)। —दृढ-ता, f. or दृढ-त्व, अम्, n. firmness, hardness, solidity, strength; steadiness, perseverance. —दृढ-तृण, अस्, m. ‘the strong grass,’ a kind of grass, Saccharum Munjia; (आ), f. a kind of grass, = वल्व-जा. —दृढ-तोरणार्गल, अस्, आ, अम्, hav-ing the bars of the gates firmly fastened. —दृढ-त्वच्, क्, m. ‘having tough bark,’ a kind of reed, = यावनालशर. —दृढ-दंशक, अस्, m. ‘having strong teeth or a hard biter,’ a shark. —दृढ-दस्यु, उस्, m., N. of an old sage, also named Idhma-vāha, (son of Dṛḍha-cyuta; cf. दृढस्यु।) —दृढ-द्वार, अस्, आ, अम्, having strong gates, having the gates well-secured. —दृढ-धन, अस्, m. ‘having secure wealth,’ an epithet of Śākya-muni. —दृढ-धनुस्, उस्, m. ‘having a strong bow,’ N. of a prince who was an ancestor of Śākya-muni; (also read दृढ-हनु, दृढ-हनु, दृढाश्व।) —दृ-ढ-धन्वन्, आ, आ, अ, having a strong bow; (आ), m. a good archer; (perhaps) N. of a man. —दृढ-धन्विन्, ई, इनी, इ, having a strong bow, a strong or sure archer; (perhaps) furnished with strong archers. —दृढ-धुर्, ऊर्, ऊर्, ऊर्, having a strong pole or beam; able to bear a weight or load. —दृढ-नाभ, अस्, m., N. of a spell or for-mula for restraining magical weapons. —दृढ-निश्चय, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘having a fixed determination,’ certain, confirmed, corroborated, undoubted. —दृ-ढ-नीर, अस्, m. ‘having strong juice,’ the cocoa-nut tree. —दृढ-नेत्र, अस्, m. ‘strong-eyed,’ N. of one of the sons of Viśvā-mitra. —दृढ-नेमि, इस्, m. ‘having a strong circle or wheel (?),’ N. of a prince who was a son of Satya-dhṛti. —दृ-ढ-पत्त्र, अस्, m. ‘having strong leaves,’ a bamboo; (ई), f. a kind of grass, = वल्व-जा. —दृढ-पाद, अस्, m. ‘firm on the feet,’ epithet of Brahmā; (आ), f. a kind of plant, = यव-तिक्ता; (ई), f. Flacourtia Cataphracta. —दृढ-प्रतिज्ञ, अस्, आ, अम्, keep-ing a promise, firm to a promise, faithful to an agreement. —दृढ-प्रत्यय, अस्, m. firm confi-dence. —दृढ-प्ररोह, अस्, m. ‘growing strongly,’ the holy fig-tree (= प्लक्ष). —दृढप्रहारि-ता, f. hard striking &c. —दृढ-प्रहारिन्, ई, इणी, इ, striking hard, hitting strongly or firmly, shooting surely. —दृढ-फल, अस्, m. ‘having a hard fruit,’ the cocoa-nut. —दृढ-बद्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, firmly bound, tied tightly. —दृढ-बन्धन-बद्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, caught fast in a snare. —दृढ-बन्-धिनी, f. ‘winding closely round a tree or stem,’ a kind of creeper, Echites Frutescens (= श्यामा)। —दृढ-बल, अस्, m., N. of a medical author. —दृढ-भक्ति, इस्, इस्, इ, ‘firm in devotion,’ faith-ful, devoted. —दृढ-मति, इस्, इस्, इ, firm-minded, strong-willed, firm, devoted. —दृढ-मन्यु, उस्, उस्, उ, violent in anger or grief. —दृढ-मुष्टि, इस्, इस्, इ, ‘having a hard fist,’ close-fisted, one whose hand is difficult to be opened; one who does not open his hand, miserly, niggardly; (इस्), m. a sword, any weapon furnished with a hilt or handle; [cf. गाढ-मुष्टि।] —दृढमुष्टि-ता, f. firmness or tightness of grasp. —दृढ-मूल, अस्, m. ‘having a hard root,’ the cocoa-nut; a kind of grass, Saccha-rum Munjia (= मुञ्ज); another kind of grass (= मन्थानक). —दृढ-रङ्गा, f. ‘having a fast colour,’ a sort of white substance, = स्फटी, com-monly फट्किरी (sulphate of alumine?). —दृढ-रथ, अस्, m. ‘having a strong chariot,’ N. of one of the 100 sons of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra; of a son of Jayad-ratha and father of Viśva-jit; (with Jainas) N. of the father of the tenth Arhat of the present Ava-sarpiṇī. —दृढरथाश्रय (°थ-आश्°), अस्, m. ‘having a firm chariot-seat,’ N. of one of the 100 sons of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra. —दृढ-रुचि, ‘of great glory,’ N. of a Varṣa. —दृढ-लता, f. ‘having strong branches,’ a kind of plant, = पाताल-गरुडी. —दृढ-लोमन्, आ, आ, अ, coarse-haired, having coarse bristles; (आ), m. a wild hog; coarse hair, bristles. —दृढ-वज्र, अस्, m. ‘having a strong thunderbolt,’ N. of a king of the Asuras. —दृढ-वर्मन्, आ, m. ‘having strong armour,’ N. of one of the 100 sons of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra. —दृढ-वल्कल, अस्, m. ‘having a hard bark,’ Artocarpus Locucha (= लकुच); the areca-palm (= पूग). —दृढ-वल्का, f. ‘hard-barked,’ a kind of plant, = अम्ब-ष्ठा. —दृढ-विक्रम, अस्, आ, अम्, having great fortitude. —दृढ-वीज, अस्, m. ‘having hard seeds,’ Cassia Tora (= चक्र-मर्द); Zizyphus Jujuba, = वर्वूर, a kind of plant. —दृढ-वृक्ष, अस्, m. ‘the firm tree,’ the cocoa-nut. —दृढ-वेधन, अम्, n. piercing strongly, striking firmly. —दृढ-वैरिन्, ई, m. a relentless foe. —दृढ-व्रत, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘having firm vows,’ strictly observing religious vows or obli-gations, firm in religious austerity, having a firm resolution, persevering, persistent, strict, firm, faithful, (sometimes used in comp., e. g. भर्तृ-दृढ-व्रता, q. v.) —दृढ-शक्तिक, अस्, आ, अम्, of great power or great strength of will. —दृढ-सन्ध, अस्, m. ‘firm or faithful to engagements,’ N. of one of the 100 sons of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra. —दृढ-सन्धि, इस्, इस्, इ, firmly united, closely joined or allied; strong-knit, thick-set; close, compact, with-out interstices, well fixed. —दृढ-सूत्रिका, f. ‘having strong fibres,’ a plant from the fibres of which bow-strings are made, Sanseviera Zeylanica; [cf. मूर्वा।] —दृढ-सेन, अस्, m. ‘possessing a strong army,’ N. of a prince. —दृढ-सौहृद, अस्, ई, अम्, firm in friendship, constant. —दृढ-स्कन्ध, अस्, m. ‘strong-stemmed,’ a plant, a sort of Mimusops (= क्षीरिका). —दृढ-स्थूण, अस्, आ, अम्, having firm posts or columns. —दृढ-हनु, उस्, m. ‘possessing strong jaws,’ N. of a prince; [cf. दृढ-धनुस्।] —दृढ-हस्त, अस्, m. ‘strong-handed,’ N. of one of the 100 sons of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra. —दृढाक्ष (°ढ-अक्°), अस्, m. ‘strong-eyed,’ N. of a prince. —दृढाङ्ग (°ढ-अङ्°), अस्, आ, अम्, firm-bodied, hard-limbed, stout, stalwart; (अम्), n. a diamond. —दृढानुताप, अस्, आ, अम्, deeply penitent. —दृढायु or दृ-ढायुस् (°ढ-आय्°), उस्, m. ‘having a firm life,’ N. of a prince; of a son of Purū-ravas and Urvaśī; N. of one of the seven sages of the south; of a son of the third Manu Sāvarṇa. —दृढायुध (°ढ-आय्°), अस्, आ, अम्, having strong weapons; (अस्), m. epithet of Śiva; N. of one of the 100 sons of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra. —दृढार्ति (°ढ-अर्°), इस्, f. the strong end of a bow; great pain. —दृढाश्व (°ढ-अश्°), अस्, m. ‘having a strong horse,’ N. of a son of Dhundhu-māra; of a son of Kāśya. —दृ-ढी-करण, अम्, n. or दृढी-कार, अस्, m. making strong or firm, fixing firmly, corroboration, confir-mation. —दृढी-कृ, cl. 8. P. A. -करोति, -कुरुते, -कर्तुम्, to make firm or fast; to fix, fasten, make strong, strengthen; to fasten tightly together; to corroborate, confirm. —दृढी-भू, cl. 1. P. -भवति, -भवितुम्, to become strong or fixed. —दृढेषुधि (°ढ-इष्°), इस्, m. ‘having a strong quiver,’ N. of a prince.
दृढ दृढ। See under rt. दृंह् at p. 427.
दृढय: दृढय, Nom. P. दृढयति, -यितुम्, to make firm, to fasten, confirm, strengthen, fortify, intensify; [cf. द्रढय।]
दृढव्य: दृढव्य, अस्, m., N. of a Ṛṣi; (a wrong form for दृढायु, q. v.)
दृढस्यु: दृढस्यु, उस्, m., N. of an ancient sage, also called Idhma-vāha; [cf. दृढ-दस्यु।]
दृढेयु: दृढेयु, उस्, m., N. of one of the seven sages of the west.
दृक: दृक दृक, अम्, n. a hole, opening.
दृकाण: दृकाण दृकाण or दृक्काण or द्रेक्काण or द्रेष्काण, अस्, m. (fr. the Gr. δέκανος), the third part of a sign of the zodiac or a demi-god presiding over it.
दृक्कर्ण: दृक्कर्ण दृक्-कर्ण, दृक्-कर्म, &c. See under 2. दृश्, p. 429, col. 1.
दृक्ष: दृक्ष दृक्ष, अस्, ई, अम्, looking, appearing, having any aspect or appearance; (occurring in comp. with certain pronominal bases, see अमू-द्°, ई-द्°, की-द्°, ता-द्°; cf. 2. दृश् and दृश।)
दृगध्यक्ष: दृगध्यक्ष दृग्-अध्यक्ष। See under 2. दृश्, p. 429, col. 1.
दृग्भू: दृग्भू दृग्भू, ऊस्, f. a thunderbolt; the sun, a serpent; [cf. दृन्भू, दृम्भू, दृन्फू, दृम्फू।]
दृङ्नीरज: दृङ्नीरज दृङ्-नीरज, दृङ्-मण्डल। See under 2. दृश्, p. 429, col. 1.
दृडक: दृडक दृडक, अस्, m. a fire-place or hole made in the ground for cooking (?).
दृति: दृति दृति, इस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. दॄ; cf. कृत्ति fr. rt. 2. कृत्), a skin of leather, a leather bag for holding water and other fluids; a cloud (Ved.); skin, hide; a pair of bellows; a fish; N. of a man with the patronymic Aindroti or Aindrota; [cf. दार्तेय; cf. also rt. दॄ; Gr. δέρ-ω, δείρ-ω, δέρ-μα; Angl. Sax. teld, ‘a tent;’ Old Germ. gi-zelt = Mod. Germ. zelt, ‘a tent.’] —दृति-धारक, अस्, m. a kind of plant, = आनन्दी, commonly आक-नपाता. —दृति-हरि, इस्, इस्, इ, carrying a leather skin or leather bags (as cattle); (इस्), m. a dog. —दृति-हार, अस्, आ, अम्, carrying a leather skin or bag; (अस्), m. a carrier of skins or bags, a water-carrier, &c.
दृध्र: दृध्र दृध्र, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. rt. धृ), Ved. seizing or fastening tightly.
दृन्: दृन् दृन्, ind. an interjection; (probably an artificial word made to explain दृन्भू, q. v.)
दृन्फू: दृन्फू दृन्फू or दृन्भू, ऊस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. दृम्फ् or दृम्प्, q. v.), a thunderbolt; the sun; f. a snake in general; a wheel; [cf. दृग्-भू, दृम्फू, दृम्भू, and see Gram. 126. c.]
दृप्: दृप् 1. दृप् or दृफ् (connected with rt. दृम्प् next col.), cl. 6. P. दृपति, दृफति, दृम्फति, &c., to pain, inflict pain, torture.
दृप् 2. दृप्, cl. 1. 10. P. दर्पति and दर्पयति, &c., to light, kindle, inflame.

दृप् 3. दृप्, cl. 4. P. दृप्यति, ददर्प, दर्पिता, दर्प्ता, द्रप्ता, द्रप्स्यति, अदृ-पत्, अद्राप्सीत् or अदार्प्सीत्, अदर्पीत्, दर्पितुम्, दर्प्तुम् and द्रप्तुम्, to be mad; to be foolish; to be extravagant or wild; to be arrogant or insolent; to be vain or proud; to be wildly delighted: Caus. दर्पयति, -यितुं, to make mad or proud or arro-gant; [cf. rt. तृप्; Gr. δόρπος.]
दृप्त: दृप्त, अस्, आ, अम्, mad, wild, proud, arrogant. —दृप्त-बालाकि, इस्, m., Ved., N. of a man with the patronymic Gārgya.
दृप्यत्: दृप्यत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, being proud or arrogant.
दृप्र: दृप्र, अस्, आ, अम्, proud, arrogant; strong, powerful.
दृभ्: दृभ् 1. दृभ्, cl. 6. 1. 10. P. दृभति, दर्भति, दर्भयति, ददर्भ, &c., to string together, arrange, tie, fasten.
दृभ् 2. दृभ्, cl. 1. 10. P. दर्भति and दर्भयति, &c., to fear, be afraid.
दृब्ध: 1. दृब्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, strung, tied, connected.
2. दृब्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, afraid, frightened.
दृब्धि: दृब्धि, इस्, f. stringing together, arranging.
दृभीक: दृभीक दृभीक, अस्, m. (fancifully derived by Sāyaṇa fr. rt. दॄ with 2. भी, ‘fear,’ and 1. कृ), Ved., N. of a demon slain by Indra.
दृमिचण्डेश्वर: दृमिचण्डेश्वर दृमिचण्डेश्वर, N. of a Liṅga; (said to be a various reading for कृमि-चण्डेश्वर।)
दृम्प्: दृम्प् दृम्प् or दृम्फ् or दृन्फ्, cl. 6. P. दृम्पति or दृम्फति, to pain, inflict pain, torture.
दृम्फू: दृम्फू or दृम्भू, ऊस्, f. (said to be fr. the preceding rt.), a snake in general; [cf. दृन्फू, दृन्भू, दृग्भू।]
दृवन्: दृवन् दृवन्, आ, &c., or अस्, आ, अम् (accord-ing to Mahī-dh. fr. rt. दॄ), Ved. piercing (as an arrow).
दृश्: दृश् 1. दृश् (this rt. forms the Pres., Impf., Pot., and Impv. fr. a rt. पश्, said to be a weakened form of rt. स्पश्), cl. 1. P. पश्-यति, ददर्श (rarely ददृशे, 2nd sing. P. ददर्-शिथ or दद्रष्ठ, Ved. ददृक्षे, part. ददृ-श्वस् or ददृशिवस् or दर्शिवस्, q. v.), द्रष्टा, द्रक्ष्यति, अदर्शत्, अद्राक्षीत् (Vedic forms अद्राक्, अदृक्षत, अदृश्रम्), द्रष्टुम्, Ved. inf. दृशे, दृशये, to see, look at, view, behold, be a spectator; regard, consider; to perceive; visit, wait upon; to see with the mind, learn, know, understand; to notice, inspect; to discover, examine, search, investigate, decide; to see by divine intuition (as the hymns of the Veda, which were said to be ‘seen’ by the Ṛṣis); to look on while anything occurs which cannot be prevented: Pass. दृश्यते (rarely with P. terminations दृश्यति), to be seen, to become visible, appear in sight, be manifested; to appear like, look like, look; to be found, to occur (as in a book); to be regarded or considered: Caus. P. A. दर्शयति, -ते, -यितुम्, Aor. अदीदृशत्, अददर्-शत्, to cause any one (acc. or gen. or dat. or also according to grammarians inst.) to see anything (acc.); to show; to point out, prove, demonstrate; to make visible; to produce (as in a court of justice); to pay; (A.) to show one's self, appear, show one's self to any one (acc. or gen. or inst.), show any-thing belonging to one's self: Desid. A. दिदृक्षते, &c., to wish to see, desire to see: Intens. दरी-दृश्यते, दर्दर्ष्टि; [cf. Gr. δέρκ-ω, ἔ-δρακ-ο-ν, δέ-κορκ-α, δράκος, ὑπό-δραξ, ὑπο-δρα, δράκων: Goth. ga-tarh-yan: Angl. Sax. torht: Old Germ. zorht-yan, ‘to manifest:’ Hib. dearcaim, ‘I see;’ dreach, ‘form, looking-glass:’ Lith. zerkolas, ‘a mirror:’ Russ. serkolo: Old Pruss. en-deirit, ‘to consider.’]

2. दृश्, क्, क्, क्, (at the end of comp.) one who sees or views; seeing, viewing; a seer, overseer, super-intendent; seeing with the mind, discerning, knowing, looking like [cf. ई-द्°, ता-द्°, की-द्°]; (क्), f. seeing, viewing, perceiving; sight, view, the eye; the aspect of a planet, the place in which a planet is observed; [cf. दृष्टि, अ-द्°, अहर्-द्°, त्रि-द्°, &c.] —दृक्-कर्ण, अस्, m. ‘whose eyes are his ears,’ a snake, (in the opinion of the Hindūs the snake has no visible external ear); [cf. दृक्-श्रुति।] —दृक्-कर्मन्, अ, n. an operation by which any planet of a certain latitude (वि-क्षेप) is referred to a point on the ecliptic, the operation for apparent longitude. —दृक्-क्रोध, अस्, m. the wrathfulness of the aspect (of a planet &c.). —दृक्-क्षय, अस्, m. decay of sight, growing dim-sighted. —दृक्-क्षेप, अस्, m. the sine of the zenith-distance of the highest or central point of the ecliptic at a given time. —दृक्-तुल्य, अस्, आ, अम्, according or coincident with an observed spot (in astron.). —दृक्तुल्य-ता, f. coin-cidence or accordance (of a planet) with its observed place. —दृक्-पथ, अस्, m. ‘the path of the sight,’ the range of the sight; दृक्-पथम् इ, to appear, become visible. —दृक्-पात, अस्, m. the letting fall a glance, a look; a downward glance. —दृक्-प्रसादा, f. a blue stone used for a collyrium and the collyrium prepared from it (= कुलत्था, कुलत्-थाञ्जन). —दृक्-प्रिया, f. ‘delight of the sight,’ beauty, splendor. —दृक्-शक्ति, इस्, f. the power of sight, the faculty of perception (comprehending, ac-cording to the Māheśvaras, दर्शन, श्रवण, मनन, वि-ज्ञान, and सर्व-ज्ञ-त्व). —दृक्-श्रुति, इस्, m. ‘hearing with the eyes,’ a snake. —दृग्-अध्यक्ष, अस्, m. ‘ruler of the sight,’ the sun. —दृग्-गति, इस्, or दृग्गति-ज्या or दृग्-गति-जीवा, f. the cosine of the zenith-distance or the sine of the highest or central point of the ecliptic at a given time. —दृग्-गोचर, अस्, m. the range of sight. —दृग्-गोल, अस्, m. = दृङ्-मण्डल। —दृग्-जल, अम्, n. ‘eye-water,’ tears. —दृग्-ज्या, f. the sine of the zenith-distance or the cosine of the altitude. —दृग्-भक्ति, इस्, f. a look of love, an amorous glance. —दृग्-रुज्, क्, f. disease of the eye. —दृग्-लम्बन, अम्, n. vertical parallax. —दृग्-विष, अस्, आ, अम्, having poison in the eyes, poisoning by the mere look; (अस्), m. a Nāga or serpent; [cf. दृष्टि-विष।] —दृग्-वृत्त, अम्, n. a vertical circle. —दृङ्-नीरज, अस्, आ, अम्, one whose eyes are like the lotus. —दृङ्-मण्डल, अम्, n. a small circle on the axis of the earth within the greater circles of the armillary sphere, accom-panying each planetary circle or orbit.
दृश: दृश, अस्, m. seeing, looking [cf. ई-द्°, की-द्°, ता-द्°, &c.]; (आ), f. the eye; (अम्), ind. = 2. दृश्, at the end of adv. comp. —दृशाकाङ्क्ष्य (°शा-आक्°), अम्, n. ‘the desire of the eye,’ a lotus, a species of Nelum-bium. —दृशोपम (°शा-उप्°), अम्, n. ‘resembling the eye,’ the white lotus, Nelumbium Speciosum.
दृशान: दृशान, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. seeing; (अस्), m. a ruler, a Loka-pāla or protector of the world, a god presiding over one of the quarters; N. of a Ṛṣi with the patronymic Bhārgava; a spiritual teacher; a Brāhman; N. of a demon, also called Vi-rocana; (अम्), n. light, brightness.
दृशि: दृशि, इस्, f. seeing, viewing; (the dat. दृशये being used in the Veda as an infinitive; cf. 1. दृश्); (इस्, ई), f. the eye; a Śāstra.
दृशीक: दृशीक, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. worthy of regard, con-spicuous; (अम्), n. the becoming manifest, appear-ance; (आ), f. appearance; [cf. चित्र-द्° and दुर्-द्°।]
दृशेन्य: दृशेन्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. visible, conspicuous.
दृश्य: 1. दृश्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be seen, visible; to be looked at; to be looked at with pleasure, beautiful, pleasing; (अस्), m. (in arithmetic) a given or known quantity or number; (अम्), n., N. of a town; [cf. अ-द्°।] —दृश्य-ता, f. or दृश्य-त्व, अम्, n. visibility, vision, sight. —दृश्य-पुर, N. of a town, = 1. दृश्य, q. v. —दृश्य-स्थापित, अस्, आ, अम्, anything placed so as to be visible. —दृश्यादृश्य (°य-अद्°), अस्, आ, अम्, visible and invisible; (आ), f. an epithet of Sinībālī.
2. दृश्य, ind. (ep. for दृष्ट्वा), having seen.
दृश्वन्: दृश्वन्, आ, वरी, अ, (at the end of comp.) seeing, a seer; conversant with.
दृष्ट: दृष्ट, अस्, आ, अम्, seen, looked at, beheld, perceived, viewed, observed, noticed; visible, appa-rent, observable; considered, regarded; treated of; appearing, manifested; occurring, found; experienced, suffered, endured; seen in the mind, devised, ima-gined, learned, known; understood; foreseen; allot-ted, destined; declared, fixed, determined, decided, approved of, acknowledged, valid; दृष्टम् भ-यम्, a really seen or obvious danger or calamity; (अम्), n. perception, observation. —दृष्ट-कर्-मन्, आ, आ, अ, one whose actions are seen or proved, tried by practice. —दृष्ट-कष्ट, अस्, आ, अम्, one who has experienced calamity or suffered misery. —दृष्ट-कूट, अम्, n. a riddle, an enigma. —दृष्ट-त्व, अम्, n. the state of having been looked at or examined or read (e. g. शास्त्र-दृष्ट-त्वात्, because the Śāstras have been examined). —दृष्ट-दुःख, अस्, आ, अम्, having seen or experienced misfortune. —दृष्ट-दोष, अस्, आ, अम्, found out or detected in a fault, one whose faults are apparent or manifest, regarded as guilty; found out, exposed, detected. —दृष्ट-नष्ट, अस्, आ, अम्, seen and (immediately afterwards) lost to view, appeared and disappeared. —दृष्ट-पूर्व, अस्, आ, अम्, seen before. —दृष्ट-प्रत्यय, अस्, आ, अम्, having confidence manifested. —दृष्ट-भक्ति, इस्, इस्, इ, whose service has been beheld. —दृष्ट-रजस्, आस्, f. a girl arrived at puberty (‘who has experienced the menstrual discharges;’ cf. रजस्). —दृष्ट-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having seen or beheld. —दृष्ट-वीर्य or दृष्ट-सार, अस्, आ, अम्, one whose strength has been proved or experi-enced. —दृष्ट-व्यतिकर, अस्, आ, अम्, one who has seen or experienced a misfortune, one who foresees evil. —दृष्टादृष्ट (°ट-अद्°), अस्, आ, अम्, one who has seen what has not been seen, seen for the first time; seen and not seen. —दृष्टान्त (°ट-अन्°), अस्, अम्, m. n. ‘the end or aim of what is seen,’ or ‘of what is in view,’ an example, com-parison, illustration, parable, allegory, type; a Śāstra; science; a particular high number; death, dying; [cf. दिष्टान्त।] —दृष्टान्त-शतक, अम्, n. a hundred examples. —दृष्टान्तित, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. दृष्टान्त), adduced as an example or comparison, chosen as an illustration. —दृष्टार्थ (°ट-अर्°), अस्, आ, अम्, having the aim or object apparent, having the scope or meaning obvious, practical, (opposed to अ-दृष्टार्थ, ‘speculative,’ and applied to the Upa-vedas which are practical sciences); one who discerns the meaning of anything or has a clear idea about it; one who sees the state of the case. —दृष्-टार्थ-तत्त्व-ज्ञ, अस्, आ, अम्, knowing the true state or circumstances of a case.
दृष्टि: दृष्टि, इस्, f. seeing, viewing; seeing with the mental eye; knowing; sight, the faculty of seeing; the eye, look, the sight of the eye, the pupil; (in astrol.) aspect of the stars (e. g. शुभ-द्°, q. v.); the mind's eye, intellect, wisdom, knowledge; con-sideration, regard; view, notion; (with Buddhists generally) ‘a wrong view.’ —दृष्टि-कृत्, त्, or दृष्टि-कृत, अम्, n. ‘suitable to the faculty of seeing,’ the plant Hibiscus Mutabilis. —दृष्टि-क्षेप, अस्, m. ‘throwing the sight,’ a glance, look. —दृष्टि-गुण, अम्, n. ‘an object for the sight,’ a mark for archers &c., a target, butt. —दृष्टि-गुरु, उस्, m. ‘the lord or master of sight,’ an epi-thet of Śiva. —दृष्टि-गोचर, अस्, m. the range or compass of the sight; (अस्, आ, अम्), within the range of sight, in sight, visible. —दृष्टि-निपात, अस्, m. ‘falling of the sight,’ looking at or on, a look, a glance. —दृष्टि-प, अस्, आ, अम्, drinking with the eyes. —दृष्टि-पथ, अस्, or दृष्टि-पथिन्, -पन्थास्, m. the path or range of sight. —दृष्टि-पात, अस्, m. ‘falling of the sight,’ a look, a glance. —दृष्टि-पूत, अस्, आ, अम्, purified or kept pure by the sight, i. e. watched that no impropriety is committed or impurity contracted. —दृष्टि-प्रसाद, अस्, m. the favour of a look. —दृष्टि-फल, अम्, n. ‘the results or conse-quences of the aspect of the planets,’ N. of the seventeenth or eighteenth Adhyāya in Varāha-mihi-ra's Bṛhat-saṃhitā. —दृष्टि-बन्धु, उस्, m. ‘the friend of sight,’ a fire-fly. —दृष्टि-मण्डल, अम्, n. the circle or circuit of the sight. —दृष्टि-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having eyes or intellect, wise, a con-naisseur. —दृष्टि-वाण, अस्, m. ‘eye-arrow,’ a glance, leer. —दृष्टि-वाद, अस्, m., N. of the last of the twelve sacred writings of the Jainas. —दृष्टि-विक्षेप, अस्, m. ‘casting the eye obliquely,’ an oblique look, a side glance, leer. —दृष्टि-विद्या, f. the science of vision, optics. —दृष्टि-विभ्रम, अस्, m. ‘the wandering of the eye,’ a coquettish or amorous glance. —दृष्टि-विष, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘hav-ing poison in the eyes,’ poisoning by the mere look; (अस्), m. a snake.
दृष्टिन्: दृष्टिन्, ई, इनी, इ, having an insight into or familiar with anything; having the looks or thoughts directed upon anything.
दृष्ट्वा: दृष्ट्वा, ind. having seen, having beheld.
दृशद्: दृशद् दृशद्, दृशद्-वती, = दृषद्, दृ-षद्-वती below.
दृषद्: दृषद् दृषद्, त्, f. (said to be fr. rt. दॄ), a rock, large stone, mill-stone, flat stone for grinding condiments upon, the lower mill-stone on which the upper or Upalā rests [cf. उपला]; a sacrificial vessel. —दृषदि-माषक, अस्, m. (with the eastern people) a tax raised from mill-stones. —दृषद्-उपल, अम्, n. a grindstone for grinding condiments. —दृषद्-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having stones or rocks, stony, rocky; (आन्), m., N. of the father of Varāṅgī who was the wife of Saṃyāti; (अती), f., N. of a river which flows into the Saras-vatī, forming the eastern boundary of the Āryāvarta or holy land of the Hindūs, and running to the north-east of Delhi, (also read दृशद्-वती); N. of several women, (also written दृशद्-वती); the mother of Aṣṭaka and wife of Viśvā-mitra; the mother of Pratardana and wife of Divo-dāsa; the mother of Śivi Auśīnara and wife of Nṛpa; the mother of Prasena-jit with the epithet Haimavatī (probably as N. of a river); an epithet of Durgā.
दृषद: दृषद = दृषद् in comp. (as in दृषदोलू-खल (°द-उल्°), Hari-v. 6509).
दृषद्य: दृषद्य, Nom. A. दृषद्यते, दृषद्यिता, दृषदिता, to be stony (?), Schol. to Pāṇ. VI. 4, 50.
दृष्या: दृष्या दृष्या, f. = दूष्या, the girdle of an elephant.
दृह्: दृह् दृह् (connected with rt. दृंह्), cl. 1. P. दर्हति, दृंहति, ददर्ह, दर्-हिष्यति, दर्हितुम्, to fix, fasten, make firm or strong, make immovable; (A.) to be fixed or fastened; to be firm; to grow, increase, prosper: Caus. दृं-हयति, &c., to make firm, to fix; to keep, hold fast; to become fixed or strong, be firm.
दृहित: दृहित or दृंहित, अस्, आ, अम्, grown, increased.
दॄ: दॄ दॄ, cl. 9. P. दृणाति, ददार (3rd du. ददरतुस् or दद्रतुस्, 3rd pl. ददरुस् or दद्रुस्), दर्ता, दरिष्यति and दरीष्यति, अदारीत्, दरितुम् or दरीतुम्, to burst, break or burst asunder, split open; to cause to burst, tear, rend, divide, sunder, pull to pieces: Pass. दीर्यते (ep. also दीर्यति), to be split, burst, break open; to separate, be dispersed or scattered (as soldiers in a battle); to be afraid, to fear: Caus. P. दरयति, यितुम्, to split, tear, pull to pieces, break open; (in the later language) दारयति, -ते, &c., to tear asunder, divide by splitting or digging; cause to run away, dis-perse, scatter: Desid. दिदीर्षति, दिदरिषति, दिद-रीषति: Intens. देदीर्यते, दर्दरीति (1st sing. दर्-दरीमि, 2nd दर्दर्षि), 2nd sing. Impv. P. दर्दृहि (according to Sāy. also दादृहि), 3rd sing. दर्दर्तु; 2nd sing. Aor. अदर्दर्, दर्दर्, दर्द्, 2nd du. अदर्दृतम्, 3rd pl. अदर्दिरुस्, to rend or tear in pieces, split, &c.
दे: दे दे [cf. rt. 5. दा], cl. 1. A. दयते, दिग्ये, दास्यते, अदित, दातुम्, to preserve, protect; to cherish, take compassion on: Pass. दीयते: Caus. दापयति, &c.: Desid. दित्सते: Intens. देदी-यते, दादेति।
देउलिय: देउलिय देüलिय, N. of a Grāma.
देङ्गपाल: देङ्गपाल देङ्ग-पाल, अस्, m., N. of a man.
देदीप्यमान: देदीप्यमान देदीप्यमान, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. the Intens. of rt. दीप्), shining intensely, glowing, blazing.
देय: देय देय, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. rt. 1. दा), to be given or presented, to be granted or allowed; fit or proper for a gift; to be shown; to be given in matrimony; to be delivered; to be returned; to be paid (as a debt, wages, taxes, &c.); to be placed, put, applied, laid; (अम्), n. a gift, oblation; water (?); [cf. अ-द्° and बल-द्°।] —देय-धर्म, अस्, m. ‘the duty of giving,’ charity, beneficence.
देव्: देव् देव् (related to rt. 1. दिव्), cl. 1. A. देवते, दिदेवे, देवितुम्, to throw, cast; to sport, play, gamble; to lament; to shine.
देवन: 1. देवन, अम्, n. (fr. the above rt. or fr. rt. 1. दिव्), lamentation, wailing, grief, sorrow. (For 2. देवन see p. 433, col. 3.)

2. देवन, अस्, m. (for 1. see rt. देव्, p. 430, col. 1), a die, dice for gambling; (आ), f. sport, wanton sport or pastime; service; (अम्), n. shining, splendor, lustre, beauty; gaming, gambling, a game at dice; sport, play, pastime; a play or pleasure-ground, a garden; a lotus; praise; emulation, desire to excel or overcome; affair, business, profession; going, motion.
देव: देव देव, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. rt. 2. दिव्), divine, celestial, heavenly, (applied in the Veda to devotion, prayer, the human mind, &c., as standing in some relationship to the supernatural world or as being of high excellence, but in the later language occurring rarely as an adjective); (अस्), m. an inhabitant of heaven, a deity, god, (sometimes applied even to evil beings if superhuman; the gods are often reckoned as thirty-three in number, or eleven for each of the three worlds, cf. त्रि-दश; in the Brāhmaṇas they are distributed under three heads, viz. eight Vasus, eleven Rudras, and twelve Ādityas, to which the two Aśvins must be added to make up the number thirty-three; the expression विश्वे देवास्, which meant originally ‘all the gods,’ became the name of a peculiar class of deities, to which the third oblation had to be offered; the Jainas divide the gods into four classes, viz. Bhavanādhīśa, Vyantara, Jyotiṣka, and Vaimānika); a N. of Indra, the giver of rain; a cloud; the twenty-second Arhat of the future Jaina Ut-sarpiṇī; one occupied with divine things, a god on the earth, a divine man, a Brāhman, a priest; a god among men, a king, prince [cf. क्षिति-देव]; a title of honour, ‘His Majesty,’ ‘His Honour,’ &c.; a husband's brother, cf. देवृ and देवर; a fami-liar abbreviation of the name Deva-datta. देव is often found at the end of names of Brāhmans, and at the end of a comp. it may mean ‘having as one's deity’ (e. g. पुरुषोत्तम-देव, having Viṣṇu as one's deity); at the beginning of a comp. it may mean ‘divine.’ According to some lexicographers, देव is said to have the following additional meanings,  — a fool, a dolt; a child; a man following any par-ticular line or business; a spear-man, a lancer; emulation, wish to excel or overcome; sport, play; (आ), f., N. of two plants, Hibiscus Mutabilis (= पद्म-चारिणी) and Marsilea Quadrifolia (= अशन-पर्णी); (ई), f. a female deity, goddess; a N. of Sarasvatī; of Durgā [cf. महा-देव]; of Sāvitrī; of Uṣas; of the nymph Urvaśī; of a nymph beloved by the Sun; of the mother of the eighteenth Arhat of the present Ava-sarpiṇī; a queen, one who has been consecrated as well as the king (in theatrical language chiefly); the daughter of a king, a princess; a respectful epithet or title applied to a lady of the first rank; a kind of bird [cf. श्यामा]; N. of several plants, Sanseviera Roxburghiana, Medicago Esculenta, Trigonella Corniculata, = लिङ्गिनी, = बन्-ध्या, = कर्कोटकी, = शालि-पर्णी, = महा-द्रोणी, = पाठा, = नागर-मुस्ता, = मृगेर्वारु, = हरी-तकी, = अतसी; (अम्), n. an organ of sense; [cf. Old Pruss. deiwas; Lith. diewas, ‘a god;’ Lat. deus; Gr. θεός; Hib. dia, ‘a god.’] —देव-ऋषभ, अस्, m. ‘a bull among the gods,’ N. of a son of Dharma and Bhānu. —देव-ऋषि, इस्, m. ‘a Ṛṣi among the gods, a divine saint,’ an epithet of Nārada; [cf. देवर्षि and देव-ब्रह्मन्।] —देव-कन्यका or देव-कन्या, f. a celestial or divine maiden, a nymph. —देव-कर्दम, अस्, m. ‘divine paste,’ a fragrant paste of sandal, agallochum, camphor, and safflower. —देवकर्म-कृत्, त्, त्, त्, doing religious acts, offering oblations or worship to the gods. —देव-कर्मन्, अ, n. a religious act or rite or oblation to the gods, worship of the gods; [cf. देव-कार्य and देव-कृत्य।] —देव-कलश, अस्, m., N. of a man. —देव-कवच, अस्, अम्, m. n. divine armour. —देव-काञ्चन, अस्, m. (?), ‘divine gold,’ the tree Bauhinia Purpurea. —देवकात्मजा (°क-आत्°), f. ‘the daughter of Devaka,’ i. e. the mother of Kṛṣṇa. —देव-काम, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. loving the gods, pious. —देव-कार्य, अम्, n. = देव-कर्मन्, wor-ship of or oblation to the gods, a religious rite in general, anything relating to or coming from the gods, a divine command. —देव-काष्ठ, अम्, n. ‘divine wood,’ a kind of pine, Pinus Devadāru. —दे-व-किरी, f. (fr. rt. 2. कृ), N. of a Rāgiṇī regarded as wife of Megha-rāga; [cf. देव-गिरी, देश-करी, गोण्ड-किरी।] —देव-किल्विष, अस्, m., Ved. an offence against the gods. —देव-कीर्त्ति, इस्, m., N. of an astronomer. —देव-कुट, अम्, n. ‘the house of the gods,’ a temple. —देव-कुण्ड, अम्, n. a natural spring. —देव-कुरु, अवस्, m. pl., N. of a people and the district inhabited by them, (usually asso-ciated with the name Uttara-kuru.) —देव-कुरुम्बा, f., N. of a plant, = महा-द्रोणा. —देव-कुल, अम्, n. = प्रासाद, a temple; [cf. दण्ड-द्°।] —देव-कुल्या, f. ‘the river of the gods,’ personified as a daughter of Pūrṇiman and grand-daughter of Marīci; N. of the wife of Ud-gītha. —देव-कुसुम, अम्, n. ‘the flower of the gods,’ cloves. —देव-कूट, ‘the divine peak,’ N. of a mountain; N. of Adam's Peak. —देव-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. made or done or performed by the gods. —देव-कृत्य, अम्, n. a religious act directed to the gods; anything relating to the gods, a divine command. —देव-कोश, अस्, m., Ved. divine cask or receptacle. —देव-क्षत्र, अम्, n. divine dominion; (अस्, आ, अम्), Ved. under the dominion of the gods; (अस्), m., N. of a prince who was a son of Deva-rāta. —देव-क्षेत्र, अम्, n., Ved. the domain of the gods. —देव-क्षेम, अस्, m., N. of the author of the Vijñāna-kāya; [cf. देव-शर्मन्।] —देव-खात, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘dug by the gods,’ i. e. hollow by nature; (अम्), n. a cave or natural hollow among mountains; a natural pond or reservoir. —देवखातक, अम्, n. a natural pond or one in front of a temple; a natural cavern, a grotto. —देवखात-विल, अम्, n. ‘a chasm dug by the gods,’ a cavern, a chasm, a natural receptacle of water or reservoir. —देव-गण, अस्, m. a troop or class of gods. —देवगण-देव, अस्, m., N. of a poet. —देव-गणिका, f. ‘a divine courtezan,’ an Ap-saras. —देवगणेश्वर (°ण-ईश्°), अस्, m. ‘lord of the troop of gods,’ an epithet of Indra. —देव-गन्धर्व, आस्, m. pl. the divine Gandharvas (superior to the human Gandharvas; cf. मनुष्य-गन्धर्व); (अस्), m. an epithet of Nārada; (अम्), n. a mode of singing; [cf. छालिक्य and देव-गान्धार।] —देव-गन्धा, f. ‘having divine fragrance,’ a kind of fragrant medicinal plant (= महा-मोदा). —देव-गर्जन, अम्, n. ‘celestial roaring,’ thunder. —देव-गर्भ, अस्, m. a divine child, the offspring of a god [cf. देव-शिशु]; (आ), f., N. of a river in Kuśa-dvīpa. —देव-गान्धार, अस् or अम्, m. or n. a peculiar mode of singing, a kind of song [cf. छालिक्य]; (ई), f. one of the Rāgiṇīs or female personifications of the modes of music, who was wife of Śrī-rāga. —देव-गायन, अस्, m. ‘a songster of the gods,’ a celestial chorister, a Gandharva. —देव-गिरि, इस्, m. ‘the divine hill,’ N. of a mountain, (periphrastically expressed in Megha-dūta 43. as देव-पूर्वो गिरिस्, and according to a commentator so called because thought to be the domicile of Kārttikeya); N. of the town Daulat-ābād which is situated between mountains. —देव-गिरी, f.
